places.name: Andalen Plantation
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 87 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A Dres saltrice enterprise with a great house, a drying floor, a counting room and a labour row, abandoned at the secession when the people who worked it stopped and the family who owned it did not come back.
why.siteAdvantages: Prime saltrice ground on slack water, with a private landing for the crop.
why.occupantsMotive: The house stands unoccupied. The fields are worked by the people from the rows down the road. They take the crop off it. They stop at the drying floor.
why.pressures: The house is intact and unlooted after two centuries. Somebody is maintaining that arrangement. The field-holder says it is the Dres who see to it, which cannot be true.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be occupied within a month if the field-holders decided the taboo was over. The house is worth more than the whole village.

hardConstraints: prime saltrice ground with a private landing
places.hook: A Dunmer plantation that failed with the crop still in the ground. The house ledgers name whose fault it was.

why.occupantsMotive: A caretaker few keep it swept and the relics in place; the city funds them rather than be seen letting the site go unkept.

why.founding: A field-owner's hired guard was stood down without pay at the end of a bad season and walked as far as the channel boom. They took the keeper's lodge. The boom now opens for people who have settled with them.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm bank within two hundred metres of the boom's anchor, high enough that the keeper is not flooded out of the job.
why.occupantsMotive: They are levying what they were owed, one hull at a time. Their sergeant can quote the wage clause under which she is collecting.
why.pressures: Every boat crew in the district has stopped using the channel. The levy is falling. They stopped a Thorn factor's boat last month, which they would not have done in spring.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would break up within a month if the field-owners paid the arrears, which they will not.

why.founding: A chamber under the Loriasel shelf with air trapped in its crown. The way in is a slot in the rock, a sump for two months a year and a squeeze the rest of it, opening on an empty air chamber.
why.siteAdvantages: A limestone void with no drain out of it, sealed by its own roof. One opening, the width of a person.

why.pressures: The slot floods in the monsoon and the divers argue about how long the crown's air lasts. Two people have tested it and one came back.

places.name: Buried Blades
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 194 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: In 1E 2836 the Argonians stopped fighting the Blackwater War overnight. In the north they buried the proof: a whole district's weapons oiled, wrapped and put in one pit, so that stopping could not easily be undone.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry gravel lens under a low rise, chosen because it drains. That is why the contents are still recognisable.
why.occupantsMotive: No guard stands over it. Four villages have known where it is for sixteen hundred years. Children are told about the pit the way they are told about the deep channel.
why.pressures: An-Xileel interest in the province's armament has made the pit awkward. One of the four villages has started asking what the other three would do.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would change the north's politics in a week if it were opened. It has stayed shut for sixteen centuries.

hardConstraints: a dry gravel lens under a rise
places.hook: A whole district's weapons, buried in one pit when the Blackwater War stopped. The An-Xileel have begun asking where it is.

why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned if one of the three trunks came down, because two will not brace.

why.pressures: The vicecanons have twice sent surveyors to establish whether the cuttings are within the city's boundary; both surveyors were treated hospitably and both reports were inconclusive.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be inside the city and paying within a year of a survey that came back conclusive.

places.whySiteWon: spring head in border mountains (danger band 3), 1632 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote.

why.founding: When the northern plain under the rim dries, every animal on it walks to the same three tree-islands for water, so for two months this ground holds more game than anywhere else in the region, along with the predators and the hunters that follow it.
why.siteAdvantages: The last standing water on the plain: three spring-fed pools under tree cover at the foot of the rim, which do not fail in a normal dry year.
why.occupantsMotive: Four villages hunt it under an allocation they renegotiate every year at Wolk Market. The four villages settle their other disputes in the same week.
why.pressures: A long dry year concentrates the herds harder and the allocation stops holding; the last time it failed, two villages did not speak for a decade.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would end the villages' year as they organise it if the springs failed.

hardConstraints: spring-fed pools that survive the dry season, on the plain under the rim

places.hook: In the dry months every animal on the plain comes to these three pools. So do the predators that follow them.

why.founding: A deep bend where the northern river slows and the fish hold. It is the most productive water in the region, worked by four villages' boats and argued over by all four for longer than living memory records.
why.siteAdvantages: A scoured hole below a gravel shoulder: deep and cold, reliably holding fish. No other water in the north matches it.

why.pressures: The rotation has held for generations. Stormhold's market buyers pay for volume. They do not ask whose week it is.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be fished out in three seasons if the rotation broke. Every fisher on it knows the number.

hardConstraints: a deep scoured hole below a gravel shoulder
four villages within a morning's row
places.hook: The deepest hole in the northern water, seldom empty. A stake on the bank carries the four villages' rotation.

why.siteAdvantages: Warm spring-fed shallows at a constant temperature, screened on every side. The pools were found rather than dug.

places.whySiteWon: cliff bench in firm lowland (danger band 2), 206 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #5 landform; won on region, landform, danger.

why.founding: An old tribal village on the Panther River where it drains into its basin, holding the western approach to the north. It has its own tribe and its own elder naheesh. The xanmeer Xal Irasotl stands close enough to be the tribe's charge rather than its neighbour.

why.founding: Stormhold built a stone causeway to Bogmother because the pilgrimage could not wait on the season.
why.siteAdvantages: The shortest line of shallow bog between the city's south gate and the sacred ground.
why.occupantsMotive: The city maintains it as a civic duty; the maintenance gang is a hereditary office with a bad reputation.
why.pressures: It is stone, which since the Duskfall counts as a moral compromise. The pilgrimage is why it is tolerated.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be replaced with timber if it ever failed completely, which the caretakers would prefer and the city would not.

hardConstraints: shallow bog between two fixed points

why.founding: The Tear road is one of the province's two roads out. A road to Morrowind needs a last stage on the Argonian side.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the road leaves the marsh for the pass. Above it there is no fodder and no level ground.
why.occupantsMotive: The stage is run by a family who take payment in both coin and salt and prefer salt.
why.pressures: Dunmer caravans and Argonian porters use the same yard and keep to opposite sides of it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a border town if the traffic doubled. The stage family can name the year they think that will happen.

hardConstraints: last level ground before the pass

places.name: Tearmouth
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 612 m from the nearest route; no free 'natural-harbour' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger.

why.founding: Where the north river meets navigable water, cargo has to change hulls. A two-culture port grew at the transfer point: Argonian on the water, Dunmer on the bank. Each half calls itself the port.
why.siteAdvantages: The head of deep-draught navigation. Below it a keeled hull can float. Above it, shallow craft only. Two dredging schemes have failed to move the line.
why.occupantsMotive: Transfer fees and warehousing. A customs presence run out of Thorn with two clerks. A great deal of business the two clerks are not shown.
why.pressures: Both halves of the town want the customs house on the other side of the water; the Thorn road wants a bridge; and the whole place empties for six weeks when the river runs too hard to transfer at all.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would lose half its trade to a deeper channel and all of it to a bridge. It has resisted both for a century.

places.hook: Where cargo changes hulls: two half-towns, one customs house and a berth of any kind for whoever asks the right half.

places.name: Ten-Maur-Wolk
places.whySiteWon: saddle in upland hills (danger band 3), 1132 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, remote.

why.founding: A temple to Boethiah and Vaermina raised by Dunmer dissidents who fled the Tribunal, then abandoned by them. The Third Empire's surveyors renamed it Tenmar Wall on their maps. The north kept the old name. The market that carries the shortened form grew half a morning's walk away where the carters' tracks bend, the closest the carters wanted to build.
why.siteAdvantages: Off the road, in a hollow that the tracks curve to avoid. Every carter in the north can point at the hollow from the bend.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it. The marker posts around it are maintained.
why.pressures: The market town that borrowed its name lives off the road and pretends the ruin is somebody else's business; the second atrocity on this ground is the Dres slave road that ran past the district, not the dissidents' work.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would draw a cult within a year if the markers ever stopped being renewed.

hardConstraints: off every route, in ground that carries no track
places.hook: A Daedric shrine ringed with white posts that were painted this year.

places.name: Ten-Thousand-Nests
places.whySiteWon: islet in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 695 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A stand of dead trees in shallow water where the north's wading birds nest in numbers that make the stand uninhabitable and the ground beneath it the richest fertiliser source in the region.
why.siteAdvantages: Dead standing timber over water, with no route in for predators. Forty years of guano beneath it.
why.occupantsMotive: The villages take guano for the terraces in one licensed month and stay away for eleven, an arrangement the smell enforces more than any warden does.
why.pressures: The saltrice growers want more than one month; the villages that eat the eggs want none at all; the stand itself is rotting and falling tree by tree.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would relocate entirely if the stand came down. Birds do; the licensors have never traced where.

places.hook: Forty years of guano under dead standing timber, worth money, but the colony above will not agree to it.

why.founding: The Dres built a stone causeway north from their frontier holdings towards the Tear road. The Argonians who inherited it keep it. There is no other hard ground across four kilometres of sink.
why.siteAdvantages: The line of a buried gravel ridge. The Dres surveyed it. The road has followed the survey ever since.
why.occupantsMotive: The holdings at either end maintain it jointly under an arrangement neither of them likes and both of them keep.
why.pressures: It is Dunmer work in a province that reads stone as a moral error, so it is used constantly and spoken of badly; three sections have been let go deliberately.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be let go entirely if the northern holdings emptied. The north would lose its only dry winter road.

hardConstraints: a buried gravel ridge across sinking ground

why.pressures: The herders who once worked for the family will not go near the stair-throat where the compound used to stand.

why.founding: A xanmeer whose ground subsided into the lake, taking a complete Merethic building down with it intact.
why.siteAdvantages: A lake basin over soft ground, where subsidence is common.
why.occupantsMotive: The building is empty. The nearest village dives it for stone fittings and considers this different from looting a standing xanmeer.
why.pressures: Greylight does not accept the distinction. It has said so twice at the market.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a serious quarrel the day someone brought up something that was clearly a Hist chamber's fitting.

places.hook: One stone step in open water. A whole building in green light beneath it.

places.name: Empty Socket
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in upland hills (danger band 3), 271 m from the nearest route; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: A small Barsaebic structure built around a single stone socket, with the stone gone. The record cut beside it says it was taken in the same generation the building went up.
why.siteAdvantages: A rock knoll clear of the flood, close enough to the Silyanorn system to be part of it and far enough that the diggings' crews have stopped checking it.
why.occupantsMotive: The chamber has been searched top to bottom; only the socket and the record remain in it.
why.pressures: The record beside the socket is legible. It gives the name of whoever took the stone. The name appears in no other source the Whispers scholars have found.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be the most important room in the north if the stone were put back. The Whispers scholars say so often.

hardConstraints: a rock knoll above the flood

why.founding: Thorn's field-owners keep a levy. A levy has to be quartered where the fields end and the road to Morrowind begins.
why.siteAdvantages: The gap between the terrace country and the pass road. An approach from the north has to cross it.
why.occupantsMotive: The levy exists to protect titles. Its officers are the field-owners' sons.
why.pressures: Half the levy are Dunmer, which is either sensible recruiting or a serious mistake depending on who is asked.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be disbanded within a year if Thorn's title disputes were settled; the field-owners show no sign of settling them.

hardConstraints: the gap between the fields and the pass road

places.name: First-Counted
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 82 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, sightline, region.

why.founding: The first ground the Flu filled, in the first season, before the city understood what was happening.
why.siteAdvantages: On the terrace below Stormhold's south gate. At the time the mowing gangs could carry the dead no further. The first season's dead went into a cut in the terrace rather than into graves. The cut goes down three levels.
why.occupantsMotive: The city maintains it. The mowing gang works between the second and fourth hours; that slot has stood in their warrant for a century.
why.pressures: Kothringi dead are buried here alongside Argonian dead. Neither people's rite permits the mixing and both accepted it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be the north's central memorial if the city could bear to make it one.

hardConstraints: within sight of the city gate

places.name: Fish Boon Ground
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 104 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: Hissmir's Fish Boon Feast needs somewhere to happen that is not the pilgrimage xanmeer. This river flat below the village has been that place for as long as the feast has existed.
why.siteAdvantages: A wide gravel flat where the river slows. Shallow enough for netting from the bank and wide enough for the whole village and its pilgrims. Every flood scours it clean.
why.occupantsMotive: The flat is empty outside the feast and carries no buildings; the flood scours it every year, which the village treats as expected.
why.pressures: The pilgrim numbers have grown past what the flat can feed. The Root Stewards may not turn a comer away. The feast now runs three days instead of one.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would move upstream if the river shifted its channel. It does that about once a century. The last shift was in 4E 79.

hardConstraints: a gravel flat on slow water below Hissmir
places.hook: A netting festival on the gravel flat: a whole district in one place, pilgrims included, drunk by dusk.

npcs: rank-and-file · single — empty most of the year
rank-and-file · few — in season: the village and its pilgrims, more of both than the flat can feed

places.name: The Flu Cordon
places.whySiteWon: ridge end in border mountains (danger band 3), 1118 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, sightline, region.

why.founding: The Flu began at Stormhold. The north cordoned itself against its own city. No other line in the province was drawn from the inside out.
why.siteAdvantages: A ring drawn at a day's walk from the city, which on this side puts it up on the rim ground, which the rim villages never farmed.
why.occupantsMotive: The vicecanons pay a marker-walker who keeps the cellar swept; she sleeps in it four nights a month.
why.pressures: No Stormhold record admits that the line was drawn against Stormhold. The vicecanons' ledger calls it the northern works.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a diplomatic incident if the vicecanons re-marked it, which is why they have left it alone.

hardConstraints: a ring at a day's walk from the city
places.hook: A cordon cellar the rim villages avoid. Dry and roofed. The safest floor within an hour of the rootworm ground.

places.name: Guar Ground
places.whySiteWon: cliff bench in seasonal floodplain (danger band 3), 52 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on route, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.dunmer-north.stands-on-the-island (+1.54).

why.founding: A second, smaller drying ground on the Thorn side, where the Dunmer holdings drive their guar in the dry months because the saltrice ground stands bare then.
why.siteAdvantages: A shallow basin that holds a skin of water two months longer than the plain around it, with hard edges that hold a herd.
why.occupantsMotive: Two Dunmer holdings and one Argonian village use it in rotation. The Dres set the rotation. No holding has owned it since; the rotation still holds.
why.pressures: The guar and the wild herds want the same water in the same weeks. The holdings deal with that by killing whatever else arrives.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would break the rotation the first year a holding brought more guar than the basin can water. One of the two is visibly building its herd to that size.

hardConstraints: a basin holding water into the dry season
hard edges to hold a herd

places.name: High Wrappings
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 1192 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The second hammock's crown terrace, older and smaller than its neighbour's. Its people will not take charity from the first hammock; their dead have been up there longer.
why.siteAdvantages: A single enormous trunk with a natural triple fork at fourteen metres, which needed almost no building to carry a terrace.
why.occupantsMotive: The village tends the lower wrappings. The last climb past the third fork was two years ago. The trunk above it is hollow and something dens in it.
why.pressures: The trunk is dying from the top and the terrace is in the dying part; the village keeps that quiet.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would have to come down before the tree does. The village has not begun to plan for it.

hardConstraints: a natural high fork over the village

why.founding: A roofless alchemical court where the apparatus is moved between fixed stations by moon phase. The work needs a clear sky. Stormhold has lamps, so the court is outside the city.
why.siteAdvantages: A dark upland flat with no light within four kilometres and a wall of rock to the north that kills the wind without blocking the sky.
why.occupantsMotive: Two resident alchemists. A rotation of Stormhold practitioners who book nights. They pay for the darkness. One spoiled night voids the booking.
why.pressures: Crystalgate's cutting sheds have begun burning lamps late and the court's northern sky is measurably worse than it was a decade ago.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be worthless the day a lit building went up on the ridge. The alchemists have started buying ridge land to prevent it.

hardConstraints: no artificial light within four kilometres

why.founding: An Imperial mission built a stone chapel on the north road and was dead of swamp fever inside a year. It was the ninth attempt on this road. The mission numbered its own attempts, which is why the other eight are remembered at all.
why.siteAdvantages: It stands on a stone footing the mission found ready-made, the corner of something much older, which they left undug.
why.occupantsMotive: Travellers used to sweep the floor and sleep in the nave. They stopped four years ago, after the mission's old cutting in the floor came open.
why.pressures: The roof is gone. The walls are sound. The Nisswo rest-house down the road calls it the failed one, out loud, to travellers.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be pulled down for its cut stone if the province had any use for cut stone, which it does not.

hardConstraints: a stone footing on the north road

why.siteAdvantages: Deep, off every route, with one boat exit.
why.occupantsMotive: Criminals with no ledger and no discipline, most of them three generations out of Blackrose and unable to work anywhere their descent is known.
why.pressures: They cannot resupply and are starting to raid villages they need. Raiding the villages they depend on has ended other crews the same way.
why.wouldChangeIf: A village retaliation would finish them within a year. The interior tribes have already agreed among themselves which village would lead it.

places.hook: A Blackguard crew living in the ribs of a barge they could not drag back to the water, with one boat and no friends.

places.name: Many-Ways
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 143 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A village that grew as a junction of walkways rather than around a centre.
why.siteAdvantages: Where four routes over soft ground have to meet, because there is nowhere else to put them. The junction is the village's whole capital.
why.occupantsMotive: Walkway-keepers who charge for maintenance and argue about who owes what.
why.pressures: The walkways cost more to keep than the village earns. The keepers have begun charging tolls the tribes using the arms consider extortion.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing one arm of the junction would strand a whole tribe's route. That tribe has started surveying its own alternative rather than keep paying.

places.hook: Four walkway routes have to meet somewhere. The shrine hung under the deck where they cross is the nearest thing here to a town square.

places.name: The Pulled Field
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 268 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: A grave-pole field where the poles were pulled by looters, raising what they were holding down.
why.siteAdvantages: An old village's burial ground, now cut off from any living village.
why.occupantsMotive: Bog blights. The grave-singers send apprentices here to train, quietly.
why.pressures: The poles are still being pulled because the goods under them are real. The looters are heirs of the village that abandoned it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Restaking the field would settle it. It would also settle who owns the grave goods. No local family has offered to pay for the work.

places.hook: Looters pulled the grave-poles and what the poles held down has risen. The cord and paint still name each one.

places.name: The Carriers' Rest
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 62 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A staging post on the route by which the bones of Argonians who died away from the Hist are brought back to the dirt.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the river route meets the interior walking route, at the last point a bundle can be re-wrapped and re-labelled before the walk. Under the racks is a cold store cut into the bank, where unclaimed bundles have been stacked since the office opened.
why.occupantsMotive: Carriers, a recognised profession and a feared one. The family pays them, not the village, so their loyalty runs to the dead.
why.pressures: The 4E produced more distant dead than the route can carry.
why.wouldChangeIf: A backlog is already visible in the racks. A second season of it would force the carriers to choose which families' dead go first, a power the families do not want them holding.

places.hook: A freight office for the dead. Racks of wrapped bone wait for a carrier going the right way. Work is taken off the delivery board. The priest signs a carrier's name to each bundle.

places.name: The Eaten Meer
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 84 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: A xanmeer the forest took: root has replaced stone in about half the structure.
why.siteAdvantages: It went undefended on soft ground, so the roots won.
why.occupantsMotive: Whatever lives in a warm dry hollow. Twice a year the tenders from the clan-tended meer come to see what stone becoming root looks like.
why.pressures: It is still settling and floors give way. The treasure-hunting outfits price it as unworkable. The tribes have stopped arguing about it.
why.wouldChangeIf: It is becoming root, which the restarted-work heretics cite against their own project.

places.hook: Half stone, half root. The floors are still settling and give way each year.

loot: grave-goods · loot-cache · tier-2 · unclaimed since the site was abandoned

places.name: The Choked Mouth
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 136 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, nearPoint, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: An older root tower that fell in and took its line with it.
why.siteAdvantages: It stands on the route it used to serve, so it is still a landmark.
why.occupantsMotive: Unoccupied. A shrine at the base gets offerings anyway, left mostly by Waykeepers, who leave them on the outward leg rather than the inward.
why.pressures: The line beyond it has been unreachable for a century. The villages it served have reorganised their trade around Helstrom.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing the tunnel would reopen the line. The Waykeepers last costed the work a hundred years ago.

places.hook: A fallen rootworm tower lying full length like a felled column, its mouth open at the broken end and going down a shaft the Waykeepers have written off.

loot: provisions · rest-shelter · tier-1 · stocked for whoever comes next

places.name: The Open Mouth
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 3), 35 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A working rootworm-line exit where the root layer vents to the surface.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm rise the root tower could push through without flooding.
why.occupantsMotive: Waykeepers and the porters who meet the line here. Neither party can price the other out; the line needs both.
why.pressures: It is the working exit on this side of the basin. The Waykeepers ration seats on it and take payment in favours as often as in coin.
why.wouldChangeIf: A collapse would strand the whole eastern line. The fallen tower two days north is what that looks like a century later.

places.hook: A working rootworm exit with a hoist over the mouth and a timetable posted as approximate. The Waykeepers ration the seats.

places.name: Ash-Fence
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 82 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: A village burned in the century of uprisings and never rebuilt.
why.siteAdvantages: It stood on the firm ground of this reach, which is why the burners came. The ground has stayed empty since.
why.occupantsMotive: Unpeopled; a bone-carriers' camp visits.
why.pressures: The neighbouring tribes disagree about who burned it. One says the Legion under Mallicius did it; another says a rival tribe used the burning as cover.
why.wouldChangeIf: A settled account would let someone rebuild. There is firm ground here for a village of two hundred, in a district with none to spare.

places.hook: Charred pile stumps in a rectangle, with the grave-poles planted inside the burnt footprint rather than outside it. Under them, a root cellar the fire missed.

places.name: The High Root
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 3), 5 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'ravine' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.waterfall-chamber-root-fall (+0.81).

why.founding: An aerial root that bridged two hammocks and was made walkable rather than cut down.
why.siteAdvantages: Twenty metres up, over ground that floods completely.
why.occupantsMotive: Unstaffed. The nearest village maintains the rope line, because the alternative is a half-day round the flooded ground and their fish spoils in that time.
why.pressures: The root is alive and slowly moving. The rope line has been re-rigged three times to follow it.
why.wouldChangeIf: It will eventually be too steep to walk. The village argues every dry season about whether to build a walkway before then.

places.hook: A living root walked like a bridge twenty metres above ground that floods completely, with every year's old lashing left hanging beside the new one.

places.name: The Basin Line
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 38 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'ravine' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, parent; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.maturity-trial-chukka-sei (+0.79).

why.founding: A rope crossing rigged by an expedition that did not come back for it.
why.siteAdvantages: It spans a root gully around which the Archon–Gideon road swings wide, saving an hour.
why.occupantsMotive: Uncrossed now. The expedition's gear is still cached at the far anchor, in a root hollow that something else claimed after they left.
why.pressures: The rope is old and there is no way to test it but to use it. The guides price a client's insistence on crossing it accordingly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Someone re-rigging it would open the route again. It would also put the dead treasure-hunters' camp within a day of the basin guides' shelter.

places.hook: Two ropes over a whitewater reach and an expedition's cache at the far anchor, in a hollow that is not empty.

places.name: The Stepped Roof

why.founding: A xanmeer whose stepped terraces can be climbed from the outside.
why.siteAdvantages: Standing stone above the flood, with the interior intact and sealed.
why.occupantsMotive: None on the roof, plenty below it. What lives under the broken slab is the hazard.
why.pressures: The route up is easier than the route down. The terrace collects what climbers abandoned rather than carry.
why.wouldChangeIf: Only a ruling by the tending tribe that climbing counts as entering. The heretic-stone dispute could force it.

places.hook: Every ground-level door is sealed. The way in is over four terraces and down through a broken roof slab.

places.name: The Ripple Stack

why.founding: Middle Argonia's pinnacled mountains come apart at a ripple. This one stands close enough to a route that people keep trying to climb it.
why.siteAdvantages: A xanmeer stub bound in root, standing clear of the canopy on its own debris mound. In a region with almost no long sightlines, it is one of the few things that reads at distance.
why.occupantsMotive: Unoccupied. Two climbers' caches and a quantity of abandoned gear remain on the route.
why.pressures: The debris fan at the base has old falls in it and one from this season. The route was marked, then deliberately unmarked by someone.
why.wouldChangeIf: It will fall. The debris fan at the base says roughly how often it sheds first.

hardConstraints: a debris fan at the base

why.pressures: The nearest village has noticed the traffic and stayed quiet. The two households who noticed first are being paid.
why.wouldChangeIf: Exposure moves them deeper. The gallery cell they supply would lose its method-testing site with a season's work still to do.

places.name: The Sunk Well

why.founding: A xanmeer's ceremonial well shaft, flooded through to the lower halls.
why.siteAdvantages: A vertical shaft in stone that has not moved in an age.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing living in the shaft. It is the entrance to something that is. Divers work it in pairs. Enough have come out alone that the pairing is now a rule.
why.pressures: The water is rising and the entrance ledge is nearly submerged. Within a few years the dive will not be possible at all.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dry season opens two more chambers. It would also bring every treasure outfit in the interior to a ruin the tenders consider consecrated.

places.hook: A ceremonial well with handholds carved below the waterline, the way left into a xanmeer's flooded lower halls.

places.name: The Bared Flat

why.founding: A shallow bed that empties in the dry season and exposes what has been lost in it.
why.siteAdvantages: A wide shallow basin with a seasonal outlet.
why.occupantsMotive: Scavengers in season, empty out of it. The same four families come each year and treat the window as inherited property.
why.pressures: The exposure window is short and competitive. Last year two of the families arrived early and drained a channel to widen it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A wetter cycle would close the window entirely. Four households have built their year around that income.

places.hook: For a few weeks a year the water goes and the bed becomes a floor of wrecks and dropped cargo. Who may take what is argued over on the spot.

places.name: The Sap Wallow

why.founding: A natural sap pool used for sanctioned communion, licensed by the nearest tree-minder.
why.siteAdvantages: Where a hero Hist's roots surface in a hollow and fill it.
why.occupantsMotive: A tender who controls dose and turn, appointed by the tree-minder and answerable to the grove rather than to the users.
why.pressures: Unlicensed users come at night. The tender knows and mostly allows it, on the calculation that a policed wallow becomes a starblossom hollow.
why.wouldChangeIf: Overuse would produce another Miredance. That place is two days away and is the argument the tender uses on the users who want the dose raised.

why.pressures: The tree-minders regard it as theft of a rite. Twice they have asked the assembly to name it, which would make it prosecutable.
why.wouldChangeIf: A crackdown would move it rather than end it. The plant grows in every cold hollow in the district; the hollows have not been counted.

places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 315 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on route, region, landform.

why.founding: A narrows where the wet-season flow becomes lethal for a fortnight.
why.siteAdvantages: The crossing on this reach, at the pinch.
why.occupantsMotive: None. The nearest village posts a watch in season, unpaid, on a rota that falls mostly on the two poorest households.
why.pressures: The watch lapses in some years. It lapses in the years when the village's men are working the porter relay.
why.wouldChangeIf: A bridge would solve it. The four villages that would use it each hold that the crossing benefits the others more, so none has paid.

places.name: The Unmade Work

why.founding: A xanmeer taken apart by its own builders at the Duskfall rather than abandoned.
why.siteAdvantages: The stone was carried away, so what remains is the plan, not the building.
why.occupantsMotive: Untended. The heretic-stone village quarries it and is condemned for that, but the condemnation has not stopped a single cart.
why.pressures: It is the clearest physical evidence of the renunciation. The restarted work is quarrying it away.
why.wouldChangeIf: Rebuilding on it would settle the Duskfall argument in public. The Helstrom assembly has avoided visiting for eleven years.

places.name: The Interrupted Flight
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 666 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on remote, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.sap-touched-miredancer (+1.44).

why.founding: A man came out of the sky here, at speed, roughly two hundred years after the same thing happened near Seyda Neen.

why.occupantsMotive: He was not going anywhere near here. The letter in his satchel is addressed to a teacher in the tradition and says he has read the great experimenter's notes and corrected the error. In the letter he writes that the descent is the easy part.
why.pressures: Scavengers, water and the season. The satchel is oiled leather and the scrolls in it still work.
why.wouldChangeIf: Somebody finds him and takes the scrolls. Whether the letter goes with them decides whether his teacher ever hears.

places.hook: A man came out of the sky here and did not survive the landing. The scrolls in his satchel are undamaged.

why.founding: A dead standing grove that hackwings have used for generations.
why.siteAdvantages: Dead timber with clear flight lines, which is what a roost needs.
why.occupantsMotive: The flock, which has used this grove long enough that the beast-keepers' grandparents complained about the same birds.
why.pressures: They take from the beast-keepers' young stock and the keepers want them gone. The tribe that owns the grove takes hackwing feathers for its rites and refuses.
why.wouldChangeIf: Culling the roost would end a real nuisance, but it would also cost that tribe the feather source it recognises as legitimate.

why.founding: The ancestor terrace of a tribe that buries high because the ground drowns.

places.name: The Lightless Village
places.whySiteWon: gorge in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 420 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote.

why.founding: A village that stopped using fire and lamps generations ago and reorganised itself around not being seen.
why.siteAdvantages: Under the densest closed canopy in the interior, where the difference between noon and midnight is small.
why.occupantsMotive: People whose eyes have adapted and whose etiquette is entirely acoustic. They trade by leaving goods and counted taps rather than by meeting.
why.pressures: Something in the surrounding dark taught them this and is still out there. The youngest generation has begun to doubt it, The elders expect them to learn otherwise.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single lamp carried in would be an act of violence. The guides charge extra to explain that to clients before they arrive.

places.hook: No flame is lit anywhere in the village. Visitors are led by the wrist along the chime-lines.

places.name: Nine-Trunks
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 241 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A village grown where nine root-joined trunks stand in one ring; one tree by the Hist's reckoning and nine by the tribes'.
why.siteAdvantages: The ring encloses firm ground and makes its own stockade.
why.occupantsMotive: A tribe that hosts the convocation's overflow and has grown rich on it, renting pitch-rights to delegations that cannot fit at the Tsoko camp.
why.pressures: Hosting a province's delegations one month a year has made them arrogant the other eleven. Two neighbouring tribes now camp at Greenspring instead, on principle.
why.wouldChangeIf: A convocation held elsewhere would halve the village. The falling attendance the Root Talk ground counts publicly is already showing in their rents.

places.hook: Nine root-joined trunks in a ring, with the houses built between them. The village rents pitch to convocation delegations.

places.name: The Turning House
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 33 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A rest house kept by the Nisswo on the Helstrom pilgrim road.
why.siteAdvantages: One day's walk from the gate and deliberately the last stop.
why.occupantsMotive: Nisswo who preach at whoever stops and feed them either way. The feeding is the doctrine's proof; the preaching is the price.
why.pressures: The Hist establishment and the Sithis preachers disagree about the interior's soul, politely. The politeness holds because Helstrom's assembly would have to act if it broke.
why.wouldChangeIf: A closure would leave the last day of the road unsheltered. Pilgrims would arrive at the gate camp instead. The guides would charge them for it.

places.hook: A Nisswo rest house one day short of the gate, with the sermon painted round the inside of the roof, to be read lying down.

npcs: priest · single
loot: shrine-offerings · lore-fragment · tier-1 · left by whoever came last

places.name: The Singer's House
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 23 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A grave-singer lives apart from the villages they serve, by custom and by preference.
why.siteAdvantages: Between five villages, on ground none of them claims or maintains.
why.occupantsMotive: A grave-singer and an apprentice who does not want the job.
why.pressures: More staking work since Umbriel than one singer can do. The necropolis village a day away has offered to take the circuit, which the five villages cannot afford.
why.wouldChangeIf: The apprentice leaving would strand five villages' dead. She has family at the Hist-less refuge and has been asking about it.

places.hook: A wall of blank poles and one finished grave-pole by the door that has waited eleven years for a family to come for it.

npcs: hermit · single
loot: personal-effects · lore-fragment · tier-1 · the effects of one household, gathered over a lifetime

places.name: The Minder's House
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 466 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A tree-minder's house, sited by the tree rather than by the village.
why.siteAdvantages: Within sight and earshot of the tree at all times, which the post requires.
why.occupantsMotive: A tree-minder and a second tender who sits in whenever the first listens. The arrangement costs the grove two adults' labour and is not waived.
why.pressures: The two-tender rule is a direct answer to what exclusive communion did at Lilmoth. The minder here trained under someone who was there.
why.wouldChangeIf: A minder who listened alone would be removed. The removal would be the district's business within a day.

places.hook: A house built with two of every fitting to make solitary communion awkward, within earshot of the tree its occupant is not allowed to leave.

npcs: hermit · single
loot: personal-effects · lore-fragment · tier-1 · household goods, one family's whole holding

places.name: Tsoko Camp
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 411 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The delegation camp used during the convocation month and empty the rest of the year.
why.siteAdvantages: Four hundred metres from the convocation ground, on its landings.
why.occupantsMotive: Delegations, in season. Each brings its own cook, its own water and its own account of why its pitch is where it is.
why.pressures: Precedence disputes about pitch positions are an annual institution. The overflow the nine-trunks village rents has begun to outrank the camp's own back rows.
why.wouldChangeIf: A tribe losing its pitch is a real political event. Two pitches have gone unclaimed for three years without a reallocation being agreed.

places.hook: Pitch markers cut with tribal signs stand empty eleven months a year. The grass has grown over the pitches of the delegations that stopped coming.

npcs: rank-and-file · few
loot: provisions · rest-shelter · tier-1 · camp stores

places.name: The Sap Road Camp
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 248 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: A camp for those walking to a hero Hist to grieve.
why.siteAdvantages: The last water before the grove.
why.occupantsMotive: Mourners, in rotation, who mostly do not talk to each other. They leave the camp stocked for the next arrivals. Little else passes between them.
why.pressures: Predators have learned that this camp is quiet and slow. The grove will not post a watch, because a watched mourning is not a mourning.
why.wouldChangeIf: A killing here would close the road for a season. The Agaceph grove would then receive its mourners by water, through landings it does not want used.

places.hook: The last water before the grove, with a washing stage and the discarded travel clothes of years hung up as a wall.

npcs: rank-and-file · few
loot: provisions · rest-shelter · tier-1 · camp stores

places.name: The Counting Tower
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 3), 32 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A ladder tower built to see over the canopy, because the canopy closes over every other vantage.
why.siteAdvantages: The tallest hammock timber for kilometres.
why.occupantsMotive: A watcher on rotation from the nearest village. The job is to count smoke and boats and report both to the naheesh.
why.pressures: From the ground there is only canopy. The tower's word is the district's distant information. The naheesh acts on it the same day.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the tree died the region would lose its only sightline. The vista ledge that would replace it is a day away and closing over.

places.hook: Six ladder stages up one tree. The slate at the top records what was seen and when, going back forty years.

loot: provisions · rest-shelter · tier-1 · left stocked by the last party to pass

places.name: The Tapping Camp
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 113 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: Illicit sap-tappers working trees the tree-minders do not visit.
why.siteAdvantages: Between three unattended wild Hist, on a creek that gets a boat out.
why.occupantsMotive: Tappers who sell to a city fence and know exactly what they are doing. They work only wild Hist, so no tribe has standing to complain.
why.pressures: The tree-minders have put a bounty on them, paid in licence-renewal favour. The licensed stage's own tappers are the ones hunting them.
why.wouldChangeIf: One arrest would name the fence and unroll the trade, including the tapped-tree crew, who use the same buyer under a lapsed concession.

places.hook: Sap barrels already branded with a city merchant's mark and stencilled for the buyer. The tappers defend the camp themselves.

npcs: lieutenant · single · named

places.name: The Poling Relay
places.whySiteWon: waterfall in upland hills (danger band 3), 396 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, nearPoint, region.

why.founding: A relay yard where interior porters hand off loads between poling stages.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the polable water ends and the walking route begins.
why.occupantsMotive: Porters, plus a yard-keeper who takes a cut of each load. He holds the covered store between the water and the walking route.
why.pressures: The yard-keeper's cut is the region's standing grievance. The lizard-steed breeders quote prices that assume it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A second yard would break the monopoly. The firm ground for one belongs to the village that takes the keeper's rent.

places.hook: Polable water ends here and walking begins. Porters are hired at the stage, where the tariff is cut into the timber with a longer list of exemptions beside it.

npcs: crew · few
loot: workshop-stock · materials · tier-1 · the stage stock of a working season

places.name: The Kept Refuge
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 718 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on remote, landform, region.

why.founding: A shelter maintained on ground the tribes avoid, against the day the tribes have to run again, as they did in 4E 48.
why.siteAdvantages: High, dry and deliberately remote, with one maintained approach.
why.occupantsMotive: Two caretakers on an unenvied rotation, drawn by lot from the tribes that fund it, a year each, with no exemption accepted.
why.pressures: Stores are rotated. The register of the year it was full is read aloud every Sun's Dusk. Fewer tribes attend it each year.
why.wouldChangeIf: Its use would mean something terrible had happened again. Two funding tribes have let their shares lapse and neither has said so at the reading.

places.hook: A capacity mark on the wall reads four hundred and eleven, Sun's Dusk 4E 48. The stores are still kept for that many.

npcs: named-keeper · single · named
loot: provisions · rest-shelter · tier-2 · stores kept for four hundred and eleven, still counted

places.name: The Fallen Nine
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 82 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.sap-touched-miredancer (+1.05).

why.founding: A trunk root that died and gave way.
why.siteAdvantages: It is on a route people still use, which is why they still dig at it.
why.occupantsMotive: Unoccupied. The bone-carriers come once a year, because four families' dead are under the fall and cannot be recovered to be returned.
why.pressures: The route now goes the long way and costs a day. The porter relay charges for that day.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing it would restore the route and settle four families' claims. It would also cost the relay yard a quarter of its traffic.

places.hook: A porter train is still under two metres of fallen root with its load. People are still digging toward it.

loot: personal-effects · materials · tier-1 · stripped from earlier travellers

places.name: The Severed Branch
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 548 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on region, remote, landform.

why.founding: A gallery taken by a cult cell because the roots here reach a tree they intend to sever.
why.siteAdvantages: Isolated, deep and directly connected to their target.
why.occupantsMotive: Cultists testing a method, working from notes that came out of the staging camp and going back to it with results.
why.pressures: The tree above is beginning to withdraw and the village does not know why. They have begun consulting a tree-minder who will recognise the pattern.
why.wouldChangeIf: Discovery would move them and lose the notes, the written account of how a severing is actually attempted.

places.hook: Root walls cut in a deliberate pattern, with the cell's working notes on a shelf beside them.

npcs: boss · single · named
rank-and-file · band
loot: workshop-stock · evidence · tier-3 · the severance method, cut into the root walls and written up beside it

places.name: The Long Throat
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 371 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, parent.

why.founding: A single enormous trunk root running toward the basin.
why.siteAdvantages: It is the dry way toward the deep basin.
why.occupantsMotive: Unstaffed. A guide camp sits at each end. The two camps keep a tally of everyone entering, so the far end knows who to expect.
why.pressures: A party cannot get back past whatever enters behind it. The guides move parties through in one direction only and wait out the day if the tally is wrong.
why.wouldChangeIf: A branch collapse would make it a trap rather than a passage. It would also cut the basin's deep ground off entirely.

places.hook: Three kilometres of root run with no junction and no side chamber. Travellers count paces aloud, on a chant taught before they set off.

loot: personal-effects · materials · tier-1 · taken off earlier arrivals

places.name: The Drowned Stair
places.whySiteWon: water narrows in lake & standing water (danger band 5), 416 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, remote; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: A root branch that grew downhill into the water table.
why.siteAdvantages: It short-cuts a full day of surface travel for a courier who can hold their breath.
why.occupantsMotive: Uninhabited. Divers use it, mostly couriers. A message that takes a day on the surface takes an afternoon on four held breaths.
why.pressures: The water rises in the wet season and drowns the last two landings. Half the year the shortcut is a full dive and the couriers charge double.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dry decade would make it an ordinary road. It would also end a courier trade three villages depend on for news.

places.hook: Four held breaths and a courier is through in an afternoon, where the surface route takes a day. The marks of who got how far are cut at each landing.

loot: personal-effects · materials · tier-1 · off the last party to try it

places.name: The Underway
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 138 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on bound, region, concealment.

why.founding: The trunk root under Helstrom, opened and kept as a road because the surface route crosses the deep basin.
why.siteAdvantages: It goes where no boat can and no road will be built.
why.occupantsMotive: Waykeepers who maintain the passage only as far as their contract runs. They post the paid limit in cut marks at the second junction.
why.pressures: Beyond the second junction it is not maintained, but people still go. The Waykeepers have stopped recovering bodies past it and have not told the assembly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the Waykeepers would close the interior's overland link entirely. Helstrom's escorted water traffic could not absorb the difference.

places.hook: A semi-public road under the marsh, floored and lit to the second junction. Past the Waykeepers' cut limit mark, the floor is root and water.

loot: personal-effects · materials · tier-1 · carried in by someone who did not leave

places.name: The Kept Light
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 301 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'hollow' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on nearPoint, region, parent; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.root-gallery-lantern-hollow (+0.55).

why.founding: A root gallery under a hammock that dropped its levee. The water came in from the back and stayed.
why.siteAdvantages: Chest-deep still water in the dark, one dry shelf at the far end and two mouths at opposite ends of the run.
why.occupantsMotive: Wisps hold a light over the deepest cut. A wader is in leech water before it is halfway to the light.
why.pressures: Two polers out of the eastern hamlets have gone in after the light this year. Their rafts are still tied at the root mouth.
why.wouldChangeIf: Cutting the old levee back open would drain the run to ankle depth and the wisps would go.

hardConstraints: a failed levee or a dropped hammock edge
places.hook: A blue light held over deep water. Two empty rafts are tied at the mouth.

loot: personal-effects · loot-cache · tier-3 · what the polers were carrying, on the dry shelf where the light does not reach

places.name: Lantern Hollow
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 79 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.root-gallery-kept-light (+0.55).

why.founding: Root gallery taken over by growers who needed dark, damp and constant temperature.
why.siteAdvantages: The root layer provides all three for free.
why.occupantsMotive: Growers who are underground by preference and rarely surface. They sell glowing fungus to every village in the district through a single agent.
why.pressures: Something else uses the deeper branches and they have stopped going there. Their best beds are out of production and the price is up.
why.wouldChangeIf: A collapse would end the interior's light supply. The nightbound village uses none of it.

places.hook: Growers have colonised the gallery and farm luminous fungus on the root walls. They sell light to every village above them.

places.name: The Root Talk Ground
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 880 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, remote.

why.founding: The Root Talk, held as an occasional convocation at Helstrom in the month of Hist-Tsoko.
why.siteAdvantages: A rare enclosed clearing at the grove's edge, large enough for every interior delegation and their landings.
why.occupantsMotive: Empty eleven months in twelve. In the twelfth, the naheesh and tree-minders of the interior, seated by a precedence order kept at Helstrom.
why.pressures: Attendance is falling and the empty places are counted publicly. The two tribes that stopped coming have not been asked why in six years.
why.wouldChangeIf: A convocation that failed to reach alignment would end the institution. Both the Hist-less refuge and the heretic builders are waiting for that.

places.hook: Each tribe's mark is cut into the root floor where that tribe has sat for nine generations. Two of the marks have been unclaimed for six years.

places.name: The Emptied Bore
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 5 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.greenspring (+0.56).

why.founding: A rootworm bore abandoned when the worm died in it.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry, wide, straight tunnel, which here is extremely rare shelter.
why.occupantsMotive: Whatever is currently living in a free tunnel. It changes every season. No village has claimed it.
why.pressures: Travellers want to use it; something is usually in it already. The bore has killed more travellers than the weather ever drove into it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing it would give the region a dry way-shelter. The guides have costed the work twice and cannot agree who would own it afterwards.

places.hook: A dry, wide, straight tunnel with the worm's own skeleton filling the last forty metres of it.

loot: personal-effects · rest-shelter · tier-2 · left by travellers who sheltered in the dry bore

places.name: The Working Burrow
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 307 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: A wild rootworm's burrow off a trunk root, which the Waykeepers watch because a wild worm can open or close a line.
why.siteAdvantages: Where soft ground meets the root layer and the worm can turn.
why.occupantsMotive: A rootworm and the small scavenger population that lives off its spoil. The Waykeepers read that ecology well enough to predict where the worm will turn.
why.pressures: The Waykeepers want it moved but the local tribe considers it sacred. The dispute has been at the convocation twice without a ruling.
why.wouldChangeIf: Driving it off would open a shorter root line and start an argument that would reach Helstrom within a month.

places.hook: Fresh spoil outside a mouth wider than any maintained gallery; the worm that dug it can open a line or close one.

loot: hidden-cache · materials · tier-2 · spoil the worm has pushed out of the root layer

places.name: The Helstrom Line-Head
places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 5), 99 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, bound, region.

why.founding: The interior terminus of the rootworm network.
why.siteAdvantages: At the Helstrom gate, where the trunk roots converge.
why.occupantsMotive: Waykeepers who run a semi-public service and a restricted one. A paying passenger is not told the restricted network exists. The register has two columns.
why.pressures: The restricted network is a favour rather than a service, guarded as one. The interior's tribes have begun resenting a road into which they are not allowed to see.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the Waykeepers' cooperation closes the interior. They know it and price accordingly.

places.hook: The interior terminus of the rootworm lines. A boarding stage, a passenger register and a second gate most travellers never pass.

loot: provisions · rest-shelter · tier-1 · provisions left against the next arrival

places.name: The Bleeding House
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 601 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on remote, region, parent; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.umpholo-mission (+1.17).

why.founding: A Daedric-worked facility built to harvest a Hist industrially, on the Haj Uxith pattern, in the interior.
why.siteAdvantages: Sited on a tree rather than on ground. The building is a machine wrapped around a trunk.
why.occupantsMotive: Whatever the bargain left there, still working the machine on a schedule, in a building no tribe has authorised entry to for six hundred years.
why.pressures: The tree is still alive and still connected. Its anguish is felt down the root line. The Agaceph sap-speaker can name the direction and has refused three times.
why.wouldChangeIf: Ending it would be the largest thing the interior has done in a century. The convocation rarely reaches agreement, but it would agree to reward this.

places.hook: A Daedric machine wrapped round a living Hist, still keeping its schedule, unattended for six hundred years.

places.name: The Licensed Stage
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 717 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on nearPoint, landform, sightline; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'.

why.founding: Licensed tapping done to the tree-minders' rule: one stage, one season, one tree.
why.siteAdvantages: On a tree the assembly designated for it.
why.occupantsMotive: Tappers whose licence is their livelihood. They police poachers themselves, because an unpoliced district loses its licences entirely.
why.pressures: The licence is renewed annually and the objection comes most reliably from the tribe whose tree carried the stage the previous year.
why.wouldChangeIf: A licence lost would be worth violence. The last holder to lose one is now selling to the same city fence the poachers use.

places.hook: One stage, one season, one tree. The licence is nailed up weathered and countersigned, readable from the water.

places.name: Miredance
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 318 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, parent; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.root-gallery-collapsed-nine (+1.05).

why.founding: The sap-touched left together in one season, walking out in the slow shared rhythm they had kept for years.
why.siteAdvantages: The overflow pool's root system had already hollowed a gallery beneath the huts. The dancers only ever lived on top of it.
why.occupantsMotive: No household is kept here now. What moved into the root galleries came for the standing water and has not been driven out.
why.pressures: The tap-lines above ground still run when the tree weeps, feeding the pool that draws whatever lives below.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the overflow ever dried, the gallery would dry with it and lose whatever nests there now.

hardConstraints: at least 1.5 km from the province edge
places.hook: The sap-touched left here in one season. Something else has since taken the hollow root gallery under the huts.

places.name: Xal-Ussep
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 506 m from the nearest route; no free 'enclosed-clearing' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, remote, parent; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.mist-locked-hollow-basin (+0.74).

why.founding: A xanmeer sealed with its tribe's Hist inside it, alone since the Duskfall.
why.siteAdvantages: A summit site defensible enough that it was never opened.
why.occupantsMotive: Only the tree lives. It has not touched the collective since the Duskfall and may not know it has ended.
why.pressures: A whole tribe watches it and has never been inside. The post is what holds that tribe together now.
why.wouldChangeIf: Opening it releases or kills a Hist isolated for an age. It is the nearest thing to a test of whether a tree can be cut off and live.

places.hook: A living Hist sealed inside stone since the Duskfall, with three metres of root out through the wall.

loot: unique-item · unique-item · tier-5 · sealed with its tribe at the Duskfall and never opened

places.name: The Coiling Reach
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 859 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote.

why.founding: A reach where the big snakes den in the root banks.
why.siteAdvantages: Warm root banks above the flood line, which is what a den wants.
why.occupantsMotive: Snakes, plus the hunters who take them for hide. The season is set by the daril fermentary rather than by the snakes.

places.name: The Made Ground
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 451 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'box-canyon' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on bound, region, remote.

why.founding: Xal-Krona are grown by the Hist out of sap, each for a reason. The reason here was the Accord: a sap-flooded hollow where the Hist made the Last Warden. The remains lying in the basin are of earlier attempts.
why.siteAdvantages: A closed basin fed by deep roots, where sap collects instead of draining. Few places in the interior let a tree pool enough of itself to make something that size.
why.occupantsMotive: Unoccupied. The Warden itself has not been here in an age; it waits in the Lost City, which is what it was made to do. What remains here are the makings that came before it.
why.pressures: The basin still fills each wet season. What it grows now is smaller, wrong and short-lived. The Unbound Root have found the place and read it as a recipe.
why.wouldChangeIf: Read first, the making record here states what the Warden was made to test. It sets whether the Warden can be stood down or must be fought.

places.hook: Three unfinished skeletons in the sap, each larger than the last, with an empty impression the size of a house at the deep end.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 326 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, route, sightline; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'.

why.founding: Somebody besieged Castle Giovesse, where Empress Tavia was held. The banks, ditches and battery positions they cut are still the shape they were, because earth here holds its shape better than stone.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm ground within bowshot of the castle's landward face. Whoever cut the lines had no choice about where.
why.occupantsMotive: Scrub occupies the lines. In the dry months a herd shelters in the ditches.
why.pressures: The fringe's farmers have quarried the banks for road metal for two centuries and the profile is going. Gideon's records court objects, but cannot enforce anything.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be a field within a lifetime at the current rate of quarrying.

hardConstraints: firm ground within bowshot of Castle Giovesse
places.hook: Somebody besieged the castle and left their ditches and their dead on the ground. The magazines under the banks are still full.

places.name: Glenbridge
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 717 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, parent.

why.founding: Pilgrims from all over Tamriel come to hear the Nisswo read a ruined Sithis xanmeer's decay as the god's sermon; a town grew to feed them.
why.siteAdvantages: A bridged glen on the last easy ground before the bog, where the pilgrim road crosses.
why.occupantsMotive: The Nisswo stay because the sermon is not finished until the stone is gone; the innkeepers stay because pilgrims eat.
why.pressures: Foreign pilgrims want the ruin preserved; the Nisswo find that blasphemous. Rectavius is still sealed below. The seal is two centuries older than the Nisswo who tends it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would empty in a season if the xanmeer finally collapsed.

hardConstraints: within sight of the sermon xanmeer
places.hook: The pilgrim town has beds, guides and a nightly argument about what the Nisswo actually said on the hill.

why.pressures: The bells still ring on schedule.

places.name: Hangs-Above-The-Water
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 612 m from the nearest route; no free 'gorge' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger.

why.founding: When the Onkobra gorge floods it fills to within a few metres of the rim, so the people who work the gorge live in it: cut chambers and built galleries on the wall, above the worst water and below the wind.
why.siteAdvantages: Dry rock at a constant temperature, on a face that has to be climbed to be reached.
why.occupantsMotive: They net the fish the narrows concentrate. Boats that need a hand through the rapid pay for a pilot.
why.pressures: The galleries are reached by ladder and rope. Every year somebody falls. The village argues about cutting a stair, which would also let others up.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become an ordinary river village the day the stair was cut.

hardConstraints: a gorge wall above the flood line

why.pressures: The rise is small and there is no room to grow. The third generation is having to leave.

why.founding: The fig canopy over the lower Onkobra is closed enough that a fringe village cannot see its own river. A stack of platforms and ladders was built to put a lookout above the leaves. The platforms are now used for a good deal more than the watch.
why.siteAdvantages: A single very old fig with a straight bole, standing on firm ground within sight of the road, tall enough to break the canopy by six metres.
why.occupantsMotive: A lookout is paid by three villages to sit up there in the flood season and watch which lanes are open; the rest of the year the village children have it.
why.pressures: Every platform is younger than the one below it, so the bottom ladder is the oldest thing here. The tree is growing out of the fixings.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned the moment the tree died. There is no second tree of this height within two kilometres.

hardConstraints: a canopy-breaking tree on firm ground

why.founding: A lashed-log causeway built by the villages on driven piles, low enough that a flood runs over it instead of taking it away. The Imperial answer to the same water was an embankment.
why.siteAdvantages: Crosses the widest shallow between the Gideon hinterland and the marsh edge, where the bottom will take a pile but no bank will hold.
why.occupantsMotive: Six villages own segments and each maintains its own, so the causeway's quality changes every two hundred metres.

why.wouldChangeIf: Would be replaced piecemeal forever.

why.pressures: A trader who miscalculates the rise loses the goods. It happens most years.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would not exist at all in a wet year. There have been three.

why.siteAdvantages: Above the fever line and above the flood. The water is clean and the nights are cold enough to keep grain.
why.occupantsMotive: Terrace farmers who sell dry grain into a province that mostly cannot grow it. The price covers the carry down the stair.
why.pressures: Grain, salt and iron all come up the stair on someone's back. In the dry months the shelf lives on stored water. Gideon's assessors tax upland grain as a luxury.

why.founding: The Orma were native to Black Marsh and gone by the end of the Third Era. They built for people with no eyes. Orma work elsewhere has weathered past reading; these ridges can still be read by hand.

why.founding: The Niben crystal workings made two men rich a generation ago. Every year since, someone Nibenese has arrived on the fringe convinced the seam runs east. This is the current one, with a claim mark, a sample pile and about eleven weeks of food.
why.siteAdvantages: A scree slope where the country rock is exposed without digging, close enough to the road that a mule can reach it.

why.pressures: The sample pile is getting bigger, the food smaller. Both are visible from the path.
why.wouldChangeIf: Will be an abandoned camp within a season. Either he was wrong, or being right brings a hundred people and a licence.

places.hook: Another Nibenese prospector on the crystal scree, one season from ruin but certain that this time is different.

why.pressures: Their ledger is the most complete record of who owes what in the south. The city, the toll families and Never-Sold each want it for a different reason.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the ledger would end them; they keep three copies and let the city know it.

places.name: Lilmoth
places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'lilmoth' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

why.founding: Rebuilt after the Slaughter of 4E 48 on the best natural harbour of the south coast, smaller and lower than the city it replaced.
why.siteAdvantages: The firm shelf at the head of the estuary, with the stilt quarters and the lighter quay stepping down off it into tidal water. Big hulls anchor out in Oliis Bay and their cargo is lightered ashore. The lightering is the city's living.
why.occupantsMotive: A reconstituted merchant council governs by tariff; it will not appoint a ruler. The last faction to hold sole power destroyed the city.
why.pressures: Hostile to the An-Xileel successor state and indispensable to a bay that must trade somewhere. It is also built over its own mass grave.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the third Hist ever spoke to one faction alone, every institution here would break at once. The rules forbid it.

hardConstraints: on the firm shelf at the estuary head, its quays out over tidal water
places.hook: Southern cargo crosses this quay. The city under the floorboards is still full.

why.founding: A village whose Hist was killed during the Umbriel passage and which has stayed put ever since.
why.siteAdvantages: Their ground is good. They stay for the stump, a relic and a grave that no neighbour contests.
why.occupantsMotive: People with no hatching, no naming and no soul-return, keeping a village going anyway.
why.pressures: Their young are Hist-less by birth, a generation for which the province has no category. The neighbouring tribes will trade with them but will not marry them, so each generation is smaller than the last.
why.wouldChangeIf: Adoption by a neighbouring tree would dissolve them into someone else's tribe, which they have refused twice. A hero Hist consenting to hatch their young without taking their name would solve it. The elders have not yet put that question to one.

places.hook: Their tree was killed during the Umbriel passage. The stump is now the village council table. Visitors are seated at it first.

why.siteAdvantages: Low ground beside a channel that changed course.
why.occupantsMotive: Blights raised by no setter's fault. With no wrongdoer to name, local law makes them the village's debt.
why.pressures: The village that owns the field cannot afford to restake it. The stake-setters price by the night and the village pays in rice. The two rates have drifted so far apart that the work stopped mid-field.
why.wouldChangeIf: Restaking would settle it. The obstacle is labour, not danger. An outsider who supplies it buys a permanent claim on the village.

places.hook: The stakes are still standing and correct, but the water carried the dead out from under them. The village has not found a rite that covers it.

why.siteAdvantages: A defensible rise in the inner swamps with black water on all sides and one poling approach. That approach is the tribe's toll. Cargo bound for the eastern swamp is counted at the stage.

why.pressures: The tribe's whole discipline was built against Umbriel's legacy, so they have not stopped preparing. Their kin on the roads are tribeless. The hold's reputation suffers for it.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the blight pressure stopped, the tribe would have no reason for the discipline that defines it. The stake-setters, the night necropolis and three subordinate villages would lose their trade with it.
