places.name: Deepmire, the Refuge
places.whySiteWon: flood high in interior swamp (danger band 4), 568 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The shelter of last resort. An all-but-inaccessible plateau that even the tribes avoid, where the presence of Sithis is strong, holding pre-Duskfall xanmeers and the skeletons of swamp leviathans. People go up only to shelter. A few caretakers tend it.
why.siteAdvantages: High, dry, defensible ground in a province that has almost none, with one approach that can be walked and no approach that can be poled.
why.occupantsMotive: The caretakers do not live here. They keep the plateau fit for habitation. Stores are turned and shelters re-roofed each season.
why.pressures: In 4E 48 the need did come: Murkmire's survivors fled up onto the plateau while Umbriel passed overhead. The caretakers have fed that memory ever since. The Umbriel Witness Society wants the memorial catalogued. The Nisswo want it let go. The caretakers want it left exactly as it is.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the argument over the memorial is settled over the caretakers' heads, the plateau stops being a refuge and becomes a destination.

hardConstraints: upland ground above the flood by 40m+
places.hook: One of the few dry plateaus in the province, kept ready since the night in 4E 48. Travellers may shelter, but the caretakers permit no residence.

why.wouldChangeIf: Repairing or breaking the works would redraw where the water goes, making one village's rice ground and drowning another's. No village will let the other order the repair.

why.founding: The Barsaebic Ayleids destroyed the tribe here and harvested its souls into the Remnant of Argon. The Hist did not die but slept. While it slept it was called the Dreaming Tree. At the end of the Second Era the souls were returned and the village was re-founded on its own ground, between the twin xanmeers Xul-Thuxis and Vakka-Bok.
why.siteAdvantages: East Deepmire ground the tribe never left, held between two pre-Duskfall xanmeers that mark it from a distance and keep the approach to one line.

why.founding: A river port ESE of the Hatching Pools, grown into a town by being neutral about cargo. It sits on the northern trunk between Stormhold and Thorn, on water deep enough for a laden hull and far enough from either customs regime that both of them use it.
why.siteAdvantages: The last reach of navigable river below the northern rim, with an oxbow that makes a natural basin, firm banks for warehousing and a rim road behind it that crosses to Morrowind without passing a post.
why.occupantsMotive: A captain of the port who governs by a nailed-up price list, freeholder crews with no tribe and no tree, Dunmer factors from the Morrowind trade and Nord hands off the northern hulls.

why.wouldChangeIf: If either Stormhold or Thorn made the port lawful, the trade would move elsewhere. If the river silted below the oxbow, the town would be a village in five years.

no Hist within the settlement — canon

places.name: Crosstrees
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 72 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, bound, nearPoint.

why.founding: The free port is built around a hull that was dragged up the bank sixty years ago. Its masts were left standing because they were useful. From the crosstrees both the roofs and the canopy are in sight. No gable in the port stands high enough for that.
why.siteAdvantages: The beached hull sits on the highest firm ground in the basin, with the canopy cut back around it so the lookout can work.
why.occupantsMotive: The port's lookout watches for hulls coming up the reach and takes no fee; the halls below pay her in beer for the early word.
why.pressures: The rigging is sixty years past its rope. The ladder gets rebuilt every wet season by whoever is free that week.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the hull finally goes over, the freehold loses its high ground and starts posting watchers on the water instead.

hardConstraints: inside 180 m of Alten Corimont, on the port's own ground
a clear line north-west down the reach and west along the road

places.name: Nine Bends
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 43 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: The gangs that work the lower channel are hired out of Alten Corimont, but the tree the gang families answer to stands nine bends upriver, where the water is still fresh enough to drink. The village grew where the tree is. The work has been a day downriver for sixty years.
why.siteAdvantages: Fresh water above the salt wedge, a bank firm enough to build on and nine bends of river between here and the port.
why.occupantsMotive: A tribe keeping a tree and hiring its own people out downriver, because there is no other coin here.
why.pressures: Every year more of the village's adults are on somebody's roll downriver. The tree has begun to notice how few of them it sees.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the tree withdraws, there is no reason left to keep the village nine bends from the work. The lower channel is left without a Hist that will speak to it.

places.name: Archon
places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'archon' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

why.founding: A deep, sheltered estuary mouth on the Padomaic will take a foreign hull's draught. No other landing on this coast will. The Second Empire and then the East Empire Company built a stone quay here. The Saxhleel town grew landward of it.
why.siteAdvantages: Estuary with a landable stone shore and a river road into the interior. The mangrove wall breaks here for more than a kilometre. No other break on the east coast is as wide.
why.occupantsMotive: An Argonian-majority harbour population who work the water as amphibians and run the port authority out of dead Company offices, alongside state customs and a long-settled Dunmer merchant minority from the Morrowind trade.
why.pressures: The lawful port holds the working customs desk on this coast, so cargo that wants to avoid duty goes round it: half-chartered hulls land on the Oliis shore and wreckers work the Padomaic beaches south of the city. The mangrove behind the city is D4 within a kilometre of the gate. The harbour authority's answer about the sealed Shadowscale sanctuary is that it is not harbour ground.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the Archon-Lilmoth-Soulrest-Tear line stopped running, or if the harbour authority lost its claim to the Company buildings, Archon would become a large fishing town in a month.

hardConstraints: deep water at the quay line at the highest seasonal level
places.hook: The harbour on this coast where a foreign hull can tie up legally. The customs desk also records where a cargo went.

places.name: The Standing Corner

why.founding: The terraces were built dry. The water came up about two hundred years ago and now stands six metres over the top terrace.
why.siteAdvantages: A drowned lagoon deep enough to swallow six terraces and clear enough to read the geometry from a boat above it.
why.occupantsMotive: Unoccupied by any household. Divers who go down have brought back no account of what lives in it.
why.pressures: It is a tended monument the village cannot reach to tend.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the water dropped a metre the tribe would reclaim it within a year.

hardConstraints: fully submerged but for one chamber
clear enough water to read the geometry
places.hook: Six terraces of xanmeer under still water, entered head-down through the top of a tower.

creatures: guardian-boss · D4 · single · on on-approach — holds the flooded core below the stair mouths
something-old · D4 · single · on on-interact — whatever the builders sealed on the lowest terrace
loot: unique-item · unique-item · tier-4
ledger-or-document · lore-fragment · tier-4

places.name: One-Chest
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 307 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; no free 'cove' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, submerged; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.cantemir-headland (+1.71).

why.founding: Somebody furnished a trapped air space inside a flooded structure and keeps a lamp burning in it.
why.siteAdvantages: Enclosed by water on all sides; the way in is a dive of about 20 metres.
why.occupantsMotive: One or two people dive in to it. What is inside may be no more than their belongings.
why.pressures: The hoard was chosen for being too heavy for a diver to carry out.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the water level fell the room becomes an ordinary cellar.

hardConstraints: at least 300 m from any road, track or boat lane
places.hook: A dry room with a chest in it, 20 metres down and no way in but a held breath.

creatures: scavenger · D3 · few · on on-approach — nesting in the flooded approach, not in the pocket itself
loot: hidden-cache · loot-cache · tier-3
ledger-or-document · lore-fragment · tier-3

places.name: Black-Cut Teeth
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 17 m from the nearest route; no free 'islet' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, bound, region.

why.founding: Where the mangrove wall meets open water a shell bar has built up and been farmed for generations.
why.siteAdvantages: Shallow, sheltered mangrove reef, walkable at the lowest tides and picked over daily by children with baskets.
why.occupantsMotive: Two villages work alternate lots by an agreement neither has written down.
why.pressures: A bad season would put the two villages in dispute over the lots.
why.wouldChangeIf: If either village lost its boats, the other would take the whole bar in a month.

places.hook: Shellfish, crab and reef weed, gathered at low tide by children too small to dive the lots.

creatures: hazard-fauna · D2 · few · on on-approach — stinging reef growth in the shallows; a contact hazard, not a creature
loot: workshop-stock · materials · tier-1

places.name: Lands-It-After-Dark
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 187 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on bound, landform, region.

why.founding: Archon's customs desk is the working one on this coast, so the Oliis run grew a last stop short of it: a channel mouth where a hull can lie a night, break a cargo down and send it in by canoe in daylight, declared as something else.
why.siteAdvantages: A mangrove channel deep enough for a keeled hull, screened from the lane, within a night's paddle of the Archon quay.
why.occupantsMotive: Half-chartered crews out of the Oliis coast whose letters of marque cover the hull but not the hold. Factors in the city prefer their goods undated.
why.pressures: The harbour authority sweeps the channels twice a season, but has yet to sweep this one; the League of Open Water tolerates the trade and taxes it privately.
why.wouldChangeIf: If Archon's customs stopped functioning the lay-by would be pointless and the trade would go straight to the quay.

hardConstraints: water deep enough for a keeled hull at any tide
no sightline from the Lilmoth-Archon lane
places.hook: The last stop before Archon customs, where a cargo is broken down and redeclared. The broker hires carriers by the canoe load.

npcs: named-keeper · D2 · single · named — the broker; keeps the stack and the tally, buying silence by the season
crew · D2 · band — half-chartered crews; will talk before they fight, once
rank-and-file · D2 · band
loot: workshop-stock · trade-access · tier-2 · cargo broken down into canoe loads
ledger-or-document · evidence · tier-3 · an undated tally that names three Archon factors

places.name: Lost-The-Ospreye
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 318 m from the nearest route; no free 'islet' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The shipping lane keeps clear of the outer bar, so the reef on it is still alive.
why.siteAdvantages: Clear water over a healthy reef in the outer mangrove channels, far enough out that the lot divers come once a season.
why.occupantsMotive: Unheld. Divers come out for a day and go home.
why.pressures: It is the healthiest reef on the coast, with no crew holding a claim on it.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the harvest lots moved out here, it would look like the Gap in 15 years.

places.hook: Pearl beds under a living reef, with a flooded cut in the wall that only Argonian lungs will reach.

creatures: apex-ambusher · D3 · single · on on-approach — holds the cut in the reef wall
loot: hidden-cache · resource-node · tier-3 · a pearl bed left unstripped because of what guards it

places.name: Sells-Their-Hours
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 214 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.wall-hist-village (+0.62).

why.founding: Households whose owing was called in are put off their ground. They camp at the edge of it because the work is here and there is nowhere else to wait.
why.siteAdvantages: The margin of a licensed sap concession, on jungle ground the concession does not want.
why.occupantsMotive: Families waiting for a hiring day. A broker's clerk comes twice a week.
why.pressures: Their ground is a hundred metres away with someone else working it. The jungle behind the camp is band-four ground.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a Chainbreaker cell reached them, the hiring queue would turn into an organised body.

hardConstraints: on the margin of worked ground
places.hook: Families camped in sight of the ground their owing cost them, waiting on a broker who comes twice a week.

npcs: family · D1 · few — D1 evicted households
merchant · D2 · few — D2 broker's clerk

places.tierOwnership: SX08 · tier-3; SX09 · tier-3; SX27 · tier-3; tier-3

places.name: Shows-The-Wrong-Light
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 66 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, bound, sightline.

why.founding: Archon is the lawful landing on this coast, so a hull that misses the estuary in weather looks for whatever light it can see. A shore gang keeps a fire burning above this beach.
why.siteAdvantages: A shelving beach south of the estuary with a bar offshore and no settlement within sight of the fire.
why.occupantsMotive: Landless coast households who lost their fishing ground and now work the cargo that comes ashore.
why.pressures: The harbour authority knows the beach exists, but cannot prove which fire is which; the pilots of Portdun Mont lose a hull a season to it and want it burnt out.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the estuary marks were kept properly lit the gang would have no light to imitate. They would go back to fishing, or go to Alten Corimont.

hardConstraints: a shelving beach a laden hull can ground on
no settlement in line of sight of the fire
on the open Padomaic shore, with the sea in front of it
places.hook: A false light above a shelving beach, kept by a shore gang. The cargo stacked behind it came off the last hull wrecked on the bar.

npcs: boss · D3 · single · named — the fire-keeper; knows where the cargo goes after the beach
rank-and-file · D2 · band — shore gang, armed with what they took off hulls
captive · D0 · pair — survivors off the last wreck, held on the beach
loot: wreck-cargo · loot-cache · tier-3 · off a hull that did not reach Archon customs
ledger-or-document · evidence · tier-3 · a tally naming who buys the cargo in the city

places.name: The Counted Lots
places.whySiteWon: cove in ocean (danger band 0), 434 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'.

why.founding: An amphibious people with a port to sell into will work a pearl bed. These beds were divided into numbered lots as soon as the trade began to pay.
why.siteAdvantages: Clear water over a firm bed inside the reef, six to twelve metres down; deeper than an outsider can casually work.
why.occupantsMotive: Diver families holding numbered lots by inheritance, with a surface tender each.
why.pressures: The deep lots pay best and they kill divers. Both are entered in the tally book.
why.wouldChangeIf: If foreigners learned to dive here the lot system collapses. The diver families teach their own.

hardConstraints: clear water over a worked bed
places.hook: Numbered pearl lots held by inheritance, with a tally book that records the drownings as well as the takings.

npcs: crew · D1 · few — 2-6 D1 divers
rank-and-file · few — one surface tender
loot: unique-item · unique-item · tier-3
workshop-stock · materials · tier-3

places.name: Portdun Mont
places.whySiteWon: flood high in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 229 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: The village grew on the rise behind the pilots' watch, above the beach landing and below the ridge line.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm ground above the flood, with a clear view down the whole estuary approach and a beach landing at the foot of the stair.
why.occupantsMotive: Pilot families paid to bring hulls through the approach. They remember when the fee was collected differently.
why.pressures: Archon's authority stops at the headland and the pilots' monopoly is customary rather than legal.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the harbour authority licensed its own pilots, Portdun Mont would be a fishing hamlet in a year.

hardConstraints: a bench above water with a landing below
places.hook: Every hull bound for Archon takes a pilot here first, so the village hears the coast's news before the city does.

npcs: crew · D2 · band — pilot families; the trade is hereditary and closed
named-keeper · D2 · single · named — the headman, who decides which hulls get a pilot and which wait

places.interiorScope: settlement: about 3–8 structures, every one enterable; the block below is the principal interior

places.name: Keeps-Its-Own-Cordon
places.whySiteWon: land bridge in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 2), 163 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on bound, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A village put under cordon during a later outbreak. No release order was ever written, so the cordon stands.
why.siteAdvantages: An island in the lagoon with one landing, which made it the obvious place to put people.
why.occupantsMotive: Descendants of the quarantined. They have been free to leave for a century.
why.pressures: They are healthy. Nobody confines them. They still keep to the line.
why.wouldChangeIf: A release order, real or forged, would end the arrangement.

hardConstraints: an island with open water on every side and a single landing
places.hook: A cordon no guard has stood on for a century, kept up by the people inside it.

npcs: family · D1 · few — D1 households
loot: ledger-or-document · lore-fragment · tier-3

places.name: The Three Tongues
places.whySiteWon: river mouth in tidal delta (danger band 2), 62 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A port needs paid lodging with a fire, a bed and a room full of people who know things.
why.siteAdvantages: On the quay front, one door from the mooring line.
why.occupantsMotive: A keeper who trades in information as her actual business.
why.pressures: Three languages are spoken in the front room and much of what is said in them is false.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the port trade fell away this becomes a village inn and the coast's news is traded somewhere else.

hardConstraints: on a route with a landing
places.hook: Three languages in one room and a contract board on the wall. The keeper sells rooms and trades in what she overhears.

npcs: named-keeper · D1 · single · named — the keeper; sells rooms, trades information
crew · D2 · band — boat crews off the Oliis and Padomaic runs

places.name: Seafalls
places.whySiteWon: water narrows in tropical jungle (danger band 2), 172 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: A drop in the river stops laden hulls dead, so inland cargo is unloaded, carried past the fall and loaded again. A town grew on the carry.
why.siteAdvantages: The furthest point upriver a laden boat can reach, with landings above and below the drop and firm ground between them.
why.occupantsMotive: Porters, transfer clerks and hauliers, who depend on the falls for their livelihoods.
why.pressures: The navigable limit moves with the season and this year's board does not match last year's; the porters price accordingly.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a slipway were built above the falls, the carry ends and the town would have no trade.

hardConstraints: landings above and below the drop
places.hook: Every load bound inland is carried past the fall on somebody's back. The porters know what is in each one.

npcs: crew · D1 · band — porters working the carry, paid by the load
official · D2 · few — transfer clerks who reconcile what went up against what came down
merchant · D1 · few — factors buying inland cargo before it reaches Archon customs

places.name: Seven-Terrace
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 498 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.banner-stack (+0.54).

why.founding: Deliberately closed by its own people, with its traps live and its vakka-stone mechanisms intact.
why.siteAdvantages: Seven terraces of dressed stone standing in D4 jungle, with no tending path cut to them since the sealing.
why.occupantsMotive: Unoccupied; the traps still work.
why.pressures: The tending clan a valley away keeps the door's location in a song. They have not opened it in four generations.
why.wouldChangeIf: If it were opened, whatever it was closed against becomes the tending clan's problem.

places.hook: Seven terraces of climbable wall, with a trapdoor on the top one.

creatures: something-old · D4 · single · on on-interact — sealed under the top terrace by the people who shut the building

places.name: Haj-Mota Wallow
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in tidal delta (danger band 3), 275 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.archon-glowgill-byre (+0.74).

why.founding: The animals that supply the shell trade live where the mud is deep and the water shallow.
why.siteAdvantages: Churned shallow mud at the delta edge, warm enough to breed in and thick with worm.
why.occupantsMotive: A small number of very large animals and one abandoned set of cutter's tools.
why.pressures: The yard needs them, but the villages want them cleared.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the wallow were worked out the shell yard closes and the district's shields become imports.

hardConstraints: inside the Saxhleel coast culture zone
places.hook: A haj-mota wallow at the delta edge, worked for shell, bone and eggs. The animal that churned the mud is still in it.

creatures: apex-ambusher · D3 · single · on on-approach — the resident haj-mota; it surfaces from beneath
scavenger · D2 · few · on on-noise — mud-scavengers working the last kill
loot: workshop-stock · materials · tier-2

places.name: Climbs-The-Long-Back
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 3), 32 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: A village built along a shelf above the flood line, until the spring above it gave way in a wet season and took the timber retaining walls down the slope with it.
why.siteAdvantages: Drained firm ground with a spring head above it and one approach that four people could hold, now unheld.
why.occupantsMotive: No household keeps the terraces now. A pack has taken the lower platforms where they used to trade.
why.pressures: The retaining walls keep failing and taking more of the slope with each wet season.
why.wouldChangeIf: Rebuilding the spring channel could resettle the lower terraces, but the collapse is getting worse each year.

places.hook: A terrace village that slid down its own hillside when the spring failed, now home to whatever moved into the broken platforms.

loot: personal-effects · loot-cache · tier-2 · left by the people who lived here
hidden-cache · gear · tier-3 · whatever the current occupants have taken

places.name: The Two-Hour Flat
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A delta flat that shortens the coast journey and is crossable only while the basin's tidal amplitude leaves it dry. In practice that is a short morning.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm sand under shallow water at low tide, marked by a stake line laid generations ago.
why.occupantsMotive: It carries no houses; six people are usually waiting at the head.
why.pressures: The window is a different length every day. A tide board at the head is chalked before dawn.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a causeway were ever built here, the whole district's travel times change and the shelter dies.

hardConstraints: firm bed under the marked line
places.hook: Two hours of firm sand twice a day. Outside that window the crossing is a running channel.

places.name: The Tide Streets
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 38 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, submerged.

why.founding: A stilt village on subsiding delta ground that the water took street by street over sixty years, until the last households moved to the rise behind it.
why.siteAdvantages: Shallow clear water over an intact street plan, readable from a boat at low tide.
why.occupantsMotive: Salvagers work the shallow end. The deeper streets are beyond them.
why.pressures: It has been picked over for a century. The deep streets still have not been worked.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the delta shifted again, the whole plan silts over and the salvage trade here ends.

hardConstraints: submerged street plan legible from above
places.hook: A whole street plan under clear shallow water, with the deep end of it still unworked.

npcs: rank-and-file · D2 · few — 0-4 D2 salvagers above
loot: hidden-cache · loot-cache · tier-3
ledger-or-document · lore-fragment · tier-3

places.name: Four-Eight
places.whySiteWon: flood high in firm lowland (danger band 3), 56 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: Umbriel crossed this coast in 4E 48. The bodies it left were buried here, away from any tree, so that the Hist could not be blamed.
why.siteAdvantages: A tidal flat above the village line where the ground could be opened quickly and in quantity.
why.occupantsMotive: Bone-carriers still call here on the way south; the village keeps clear.
why.pressures: The dead here were stripped, so there are no name-goods to carry home.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a way were found to return even one of them, the Umbriel Witness Society gains its first real relic.

hardConstraints: ground that can be opened in quantity
places.hook: A grave mound raised over the Umbriel dead of 4E 48, with no name on it and a cut in the ground that can still be opened.

creatures: something-old · D2 · few · on on-interact — what Umbriel left in the bodies it did not finish
loot: grave-goods · loot-cache · tier-2

places.name: Still-Water Sleeping-Tree
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 3), 472 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.owing-hiring-camp (+0.62).

why.founding: The Hist opened a break in the canopy on a firm rise at the marsh edge and the village that answered it stood there for generations.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm rise where the fringe marsh met the jungle wall, with fresh water and a canopy break the Hist made itself.
why.occupantsMotive: No household has lived here since the still water rose over the sleeping tree and the xanmeer beneath it.
why.pressures: A guardian holds the drowned chamber under the tree and keeps to what is left of the village.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the water ever drained, the tree and the xanmeer beneath it would be exposed for the first time in living memory.

hardConstraints: a living Hist with a canopy break
places.hook: The village's sleeping Hist and the xanmeer beneath it stand under still water. A guardian holds the flooded chamber.
